subject: Shared home-office layouts
hook: From kitchen table to a proper office for two.
ig:
From kitchen table to a proper office for two. Here's how a typical spare-room conversion runs.

The first question isn't about furniture. It's: are you both home on the same days? If so, you need two full workstations and some separation for calls. If you alternate, one generous desk with split storage can be enough.

After that, the room does the talking. The window decides who gets daylight without screen glare. The radiator decides where a tall shelf can't go. Socket positions decide where cable routes run.

Then it's our usual process: 3D design, itemised quote, manufacture in our own workshop, and fitting by our own team.

Still working off the kitchen table? DM us 'OFFICE' with your room size and we'll share some layout ideas.
fb:
Still sharing the kitchen table as a desk? You're not the only one.

This carousel walks through how a typical spare-room-to-office project runs for two people. The big question comes first: are you both working from home on the same days? Then the room itself — window, radiator and sockets — decides the layout.

We design it with you in 3D, make it in our Hanley workshop and fit it ourselves. Have a look at our home office desks for more.

alt: Six frames: a survey sketch, a 3D design on a laptop, a desk assembled in a workshop, desk installation and a finished box-room office (AI concept images).
on_asset: F1: The brief — Who works from home, on which days, and who's on calls. Two people in on the same day needs a different plan from alternate days. | F2: The survey — We measure the room and note the window, radiator and sockets. Glare on screens and cold spots both shape where desks go. | F3: The layout — A typical plan puts one desk under the window and one on the side wall, so both get daylight without screen glare. | F4: Workshop — Desktops, pedestals and shelving cut, edged, drilled and assembled in our Hanley workshop, checked before they leave. | F5: Install — Fitted to the walls by our own team, with cable routes at each seat. | F6: Handover — Two workstations, own drawers each, one shared shelf. Concept images throughout.
